ArXiv cs.AI.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26663v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative AI has improved individual productivity, but whether adding a plurality of AI partners helps or hurts remains open. We crossed AI partnership (one versus two) with behavioral formation (calibrated to average human behavior versus customized by the participant) in a brainstorming experiment ($N$=168) with human-human dyads as reference. Two-AI rooms posted more ideas to the shared board, but human-authored ideas dropped substantially. With one AI partner, formation mattered: humans paired with an average-calibrated AI posted more than

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Coherence by Construction: Synthesizing CTI Knowledge Graphs and the Formal Limits of Coherence Validation
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26717v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthesizing relational training data such as knowledge graphs with a large language model typically emits structured objects one at a time, which keeps each object valid but leaves the relationships between them ungrounded. We study an alternative paradigm, generation by simulation: rather than describing a relational artifact, we simulate a process that produces it and take the artifact to be its causal record. Language-model agents propose intent and a deterministic referee resolves outcomes against an explicit world model, so a relation is e

ArXiv cs.AI.title: TOUMAII: A 4.5M-Pair Tool-Calling Preference Dataset and Its Source-Agnostic Generator
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26722v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: To autonomously execute multi-step tasks, enterprise agents must reliably interact with tools, call APIs, or query databases, making tool-calling a fundamental capability of AI models. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) optimises for producing the correct call, but never contrasts it with a plausible incorrect one. In an environment where even a minor formatting error can invalidate a call and an incorrect decision can derail the interaction, direct preference optimisation (DPO) targets exactly this contrast. DPO, therefore, requires preference pairs

ArXiv cs.AI.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26782v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation resolves atomic-scale motion and predicts the structural, mechanical, and dynamic properties of materials, making it cen- tral to materials design and discovery. Yet an MD study requires an expert-driven workflow: designing the simulation, writing reliable input scripts, executing them, and analyzing the results with separate tools. Here we present ChatAtom, a multi-agent large language model system that translates a natural-language request into a complete MD workflow without the user writing input scripts or

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26794v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Readouts of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), such as CD8+ T-cell density, intra-epithelial infiltration and the Ki67 index, combine tissue architecture from H&E with cell phenotypes from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF). Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) could automate these readouts with an explanation, but two gaps remain. Pathology MLLMs read H&E alone, while these readouts need the cell phenotypes that mIF measures. And their reasoning has no step-level truth to be checked against, so R1-style reinforcement learning rewards

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26797v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative models now write working code, produce realistic images, and hold long conversations, yet the mechanisms behind their intelligence still evade our understanding. This thesis explores that puzzle through Associative Memory (AM), in which patterns are stored as energy minima and retrieved through attractor dynamics. Beyond their capacity, AMs form new minima known as spurious states, long regarded as a failure of memory. We argue that this failure is where creativity begins, and that memorization and generalization can coexist as outcom

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Beyond Demographic Discrimination: Benchmarking Normative-Descriptive Calibration in LLMs
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26870v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in socially consequential settings, where they must distinguish between normative reasoning (what should happen) and descriptive reasoning (what is likely to happen). Most fairness benchmarks evaluate demographic discrimination under a single reasoning objective, and none we know of tests whether a model treats the same item differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Towards Robust Partial-Edit Deepfake Localization: An edit and Generator Conditioned Analysis
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26903v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Partial-edit deepfake localization aims to identify manipulated regions within otherwise authentic speech. Recent systems report strong overall results, but aggregate scores do not reveal whether this performance holds across different editing conditions. In this work, we present an edit- and generator-conditioned analysis of Segment-Aware Localization (SAL) using WavLM-Large and XLS-R representations on the VoiceCraft and SSR-Speech subsets of PartialEdit. We categorize edits along three transcript-derived axes, namely content, meaning change,

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26906v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) theorem solvers differ in both proving capability and inference cost. Applying an expensive solver to every subgoal wastes computation when cheaper models are sufficient, while always starting from the cheapest solver wastes attempts on subgoals that require stronger models. We present BudgetPV, an agentic budget-aware predict-and-verify system that allocates computation across unresolved subgoals and heterogeneous LLM solvers. BudgetPV uses a cross-solver predictor to guide solver selection for each subgoal and revise

ArXiv cs.AI.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26910v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are expected to improve themselves from their own experience across episodes, with fixed weights. Self-improvement in an embodied world cannot be read from one measure. Existing benchmarks measure task progress, world-knowledge question answering (QA), and episodic memory, but a correct answer does not show that the agent ever observed the evidence for it, and progress does not show what the agent learned. We introduce AstronautBench, which measures one agent's self-improvement through three views on the same run: what it knows, wheth

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Self-Evolving Beyond Human-Crafted Experience for EDA Scripting
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26912v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The growing complexity of electronic systems demands efficient design flows, yet EDA scripting remains a bottleneck: proprietary APIs are sparsely documented, and errors often appear as silent failures or cryptic exceptions. Hand-crafted knowledge helps but is difficult to maintain as toolchains evolve. We present ZhuLong-SE (Self-Evolution), an execution-grounded LLM agent that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces. Building on ZhuLong, it enhances the task-level harness with API retrieval, documentation responses, isolated sandbox e

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: How much information relevant to predicting the future of a passage (i.e. predictive information) is carried by the preceding text, and how is this information distributed along that history? These questions are fundamental to understanding both the statistical structure of language and what large language models (LLMs) can learn about it. Indeed, LLMs trained to predict the next token in text must exploit this predictive information, so its organization determines how the structure of language becomes available to the model to learn. We develop

ArXiv cs.AI.title: CodeReviewBench: An Automated Benchmark for Evaluating the Software Factory
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI agents ship more code with minimal human oversight, code review becomes the critical quality-control checkpoint -- but one without a reliable, objective verifier: review quality is nuanced and ultimately a judgment call by the PR author. Existing benchmarks are structurally misaligned with this: annotators are third-party reviewers, like the bots they evaluate, not the PR authors who actually decide what to fix. They also rely on small, static issue sets that require full re-evaluation as tools update, limiting how frequently progress can

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Keep the Process, Change the Supplier: Runtime Governance for Tool-Using AI Agents
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26966v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tool-using AI agents propose actions whose authorization and external effects cannot be inferred from generated text alone. We study an execution boundary that separates agent proposals from business-controlled authority, context disclosure, and supplier selection. The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) mediates capability calls and records uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without returning an acceptable reply. We evaluate this runtime with scripted requests and synthetic suppliers: 2,400 fault episodes across four policies, 60 p

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Right Numbers, Wrong Story: When LLMs Narrate Financial Changes Beyond Their Inputs
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.26968v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A financial report drafted by an LLM can state every number correctly but still go beyond its input, adding judgments and causes that no one supplied. We call these additions unsupported framing and find them far more often in LLM drafts than in reports written by proInput facts Revenue +3% Higher prices 10-K filings Revenue increased 3% on higher prices. 10-K writer Revenue surged 3% on higher prices, due to strong demand. ArXiv cs.LG.title: On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26671v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While the critical points of the loss landscape in linear neural networks have been extensively studied since the seminal work of Baldi \& Hornik in the late 1980s, a description of this landscape at an intermediate or global scale is still lacking. Such a characterization is crucial, particularly as a substantial body of literature indicates that gradient descent circumvents critical points. The present article introduces an intermediate structure, termed the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and exhibits key geometric pro

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Parasite Features: Causal Abstraction Through Spurious Pathways
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26711v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Causal Abstraction defines a notion of \emph{equivalence} between a neural network and an algorithm, thus serving as a powerful framework for mechanistic interpretability. In this paper, however, we show the existence of a class of \emph{spurious features} which straightforwardly pass such equivalence tests. Suppose there are two directions in a model's representation space where: (i) one discriminates the input based on some feature, and (ii) the other steers the model towards a certain output. Interpretability methods based on Causal Abstracti

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Cross-Attack Robust Aggregation for Federated Learning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Federated learning (FL) lets resource-constrained IoT and edge devices train a shared model without exchanging raw data, but compromised or faulty devices can poison the global model. Existing robust aggregators each fail in some regime: naive averaging (FedAvg) collapses under high-magnitude attacks, whereas distance- and statistics-based defenses (Krum, median, trimmed mean) sacrifice accuracy on non-IID data and remain vulnerable to stealthy attacks. We present FedTether, which reweights client updates by their deviation from a coordinatewise

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Depth-Linked Residual Tokens for Multimodal Retrieval and Generation
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26752v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Iterative architectures such as looped language models improve parameter efficiency and reasoning capacity of transformers, yet their sequential backbone iterations introduce substantial computational latency. Conversely, parallelizable learnable special tokens (such as the register tokens in Vision Transformer) enable efficient single-pass inference, but often suffer from the absence of sequential refinement and exhibit redundant representations across tokens. To address these challenges, we introduce Depth-Linked Residual Tokens (DepThink), an

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Who Should Verify? Reviewer Selection with Partial Information and Outcome Audits
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26770v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Selecting an AI reviewer requires evidence about what it does after reading a draft. On a fixed batch of items, a team can keep the original answers or adopt one reviewer's answers throughout. We ask how much it costs to certify that the chosen procedure falls at most a specified number of correct answers short of the best available procedure, for every completion of the unobserved evidence. When all reviews are available and only verified answer keys cost money, we give an exact stopping rule and an integer program for the cheapest certificate

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Don't Discard Your Rollouts: Reusing Teacher RL Traces for Student Distillation
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26803v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: RL post-training methods such as PPO and GRPO are computationally expensive, with substantial resources devoted to sampling rollouts, which contain multiple completions per prompt along with their respective rewards. Canonical distillation, however, discards these traces and uses more compute to regenerate data from the final teacher. We ask if and how we can reuse the saved teacher RL rollouts to distil student models. ArXiv cs.LG.title: LEAN: Library-Based Adaptation for Asynchronous, Federated Fine-Tuning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26805v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Federated fine-tuning of foundation models with low-rank adapters (LoRA) is typically reconciled by averaging locally trained adapters. In cross-device settings, where participants hold heterogeneous data and join or leave asynchronously, averaging is poorly suited: locally trained adapters are not identifiable up to permutation, and averages of adapters trained on dissimilar data can be uninformative or unstable. We propose a simple idea called federated library-based adaptation (LEAN), which replaces averaging altogether. The server maintains

ArXiv cs.LG.title: NitroGen: Observations on the Action Dynamics, Visual Instruction Following, and Spatial Exploration
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26807v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: NitroGen is an open vision-action foundation model for game control. It is trained by behavior cloning on online gameplay videos. In this paper, we study the frozen controller in Hollow Knight and Trackmania as examples along three dimensions: action adaptation, visual instruction following, and spatial exploration. Our results indicate that NitroGen can adapt its actions to local context, but it lacks the planning, recovery, and exploration needed for longer-horizon game control.

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Realistic Robustness Evaluation of Tabular Data Driven Models
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26818v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The increasing adoption of Machine Learning (ML) models in high-stakes applications has raised critical concerns regarding their robustness against adversarial attacks. While extensive research has focused on adversarial example generation in image and text domains, the study of such examples in tabular data remains comparatively limited, despite its widespread use in real-world systems. This work introduces AURORA, a modular, open-source tool for evaluating the robustness of ML models on tabular data classification. It integrates multiple adver

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Graph-XGB: A Hybrid GNN Framework for Outdoor-to-Indoor 5G Signal Reconstruction via Aerial-Only UAV RF Sensing
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26828v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Delivering robust In-Building Coverage (IBC) is critically impeded by severe Outdoor-to-Indoor (O2I) attenuation, a constraint that intensifies as deployments move from 5G mid-band towards mmWave and prospective 6G sub-THz carriers, where losses of 60-80 dB have been reported across modern building envelopes. While Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) offer scalable exterior RF sensing platforms, a fundamental inversion problem persists: interior 3D signal states cannot be directly sampled from constrained exterior flight paths. This paper proposes G

ArXiv cs.LG.title: A Sparsity Analysis of Traffic Forecasting Architectures: How Much Missing Data is Too Much?
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26847v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Traffic forecasting models are typically evaluated under ideal conditions with complete data. This evaluation does not reflect the frequent sensor failures and communication outages common in real-world deployments. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of multivariate traffic prediction models to evaluate their performance under varying levels of sensor data loss during inference. We benchmark several architectural paradigms, including graph neural networks, attention-based Transformers, and selective state-space models, across sparsity

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Self-Supervised Learning with Recursive Quadrature Filters for Neural Time Series
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26856v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop self-supervised methods for training Recursive Quadrature Filter (RQF) encoders on unlabeled time series. RQFs are biologically motivated, complex-valued temporal filters that form a special class of diagonal state-space models (SSMs). Each RQF acts as a band-pass filter whose selectivity is determined by two learnable parameters: its tuning frequency and bandwidth. We separately introduce a self-supervised learning objective based on prediction error; the encoder is trained so that its current state predicts its own future activity.

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Multi-Tier Edge Triage: Optimizing Latency for Safe Clinical Agents
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26914v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deploying generative AI agents in enterprise clinical workflows requires enforcing multi-dimensional safety and compliance policies--preventing HIPAA Protected Health Information (PHI) exposure, maintaining clinical scope-of-practice boundaries, ensuring patient-appropriate reading comprehension, and preserving brand integrity--under interactive latency constraints. Synchronous outbound calls to cloud Large Language Model (LLM) judges add substantial network and decoding overhead onto the critical response path. We present Multi-Tier Edge Triage

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Large Reported CHB-MIT Adaptation Gains Disappear with Pretrained Encoders and Matched Probes
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26929v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dani and Liebe (2026) (DL) report that adapting the final encoder block of BIOT and CBraMod with self-supervised learning (SSL) improves CHB-MIT seizure-detection ROC-AUC by 36.2 and 29.5 points over linear probing. We investigate these results with their released code and an independent pipeline. The release loads pretrained weights for adaptation only when an otherwise unset configuration key is supplied, and its CBraMod probe reads the reconstruction head with dropout active. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Improving the Optimisation Landscape for Particle Mixtures
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.26931v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Several methods in statistics and machine learning represent a predictive distribution as an equally weighted mixture of models, or particles, trained via the mixture predictive likelihood. However, we prove that the mixture predictive likelihood is poorly suited to gradient-based optimisation, because it does not identify how the mixture is decomposed across particles, so that a poorly matched particle can be starved of training signal.
